body.en:
Question B-001-016-009.

Why the correct answer is right: Fast-scan television on 145 MHz is prohibited because 145 MHz is in the 144 MHz to 148 MHz band where the bank gives a 30 kHz maximum, and the bank treats fast-scan ATV as too wide for that limit.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "FT8 on 14.074 MHz": FT8 is a narrow digital mode; the wider bank says many FT8 contacts fit in the space needed for one SSB transmission, so this is not the wide-signal problem.
- sourceIndex 2: "Morse radiotelegraphy (CW) on 10.145 MHz": CW is the narrowest of the CW/SSB/FM ordering taught in the bank and fits the narrow-band context at 10.145 MHz.
- sourceIndex 3: "Fast-scan television (ATV) on 440 MHz": 440 MHz is outside the 144 MHz to 148 MHz band with the 30 kHz limit tested here, and the bank's prohibited fast-scan ATV example in this item is the 145 MHz case.
